audit.title: Supported Networks

dimensions.name: Answer-first extractability
dimensions.analysis: Weak. The implied question "which networks does ACE support?" is never answered — the two answer-bearing sections contain zero content. A lifted chunk gives an engine a promise with no data.

dimensions.name: Structural scannability & chunkability
dimensions.analysis: Mechanically clean (3 headings, 1 H1, 0 level skips per measured facts) but the measured `0 table(s), 0 bullet(s)` under two network headings is the core defect — a network list is exactly where a table is mandatory.

dimensions.name: Concrete statistics & specifics
dimensions.analysis: Poor. 3 numerals, 0 with units, 0 hex identifiers, no chain selectors, no chain IDs, no network names. For a networks reference this is the most damaging gap.

dimensions.name: Citations & authoritative references
dimensions.analysis: Only 1 internal link (`llms.txt`), 0 external. No link to a chain-selector registry or CCIP network directory.

dimensions.name: Quotable canonical definitions
dimensions.analysis: Strong. "A **chain selector** is Chainlink's unique numeric identifier for each blockchain network… globally unique across all supported networks" is self-contained and verbatim-liftable.

dimensions.name: Machine-readability & metadata
dimensions.analysis: Weak. Measured `JSON-LD: 0`, `canonical: MISSING`, no `dateModified` in schema — though a visible `Last Updated: 2026-05-26` appears in body text (a freshness signal, but not machine-structured).

dimensions.name: Code completeness & agent-runnability
dimensions.analysis: Not applicable — this page type needs a table, not code snippets. Scored neutral.

dimensions.name: Query/intent coverage
dimensions.analysis: Weak. Title matches intent but the body answers nothing; no "What networks does ACE support?" phrasing, no per-network status detail agents need.

dimensions.name: Clarity, fluency & terminology consistency
dimensions.analysis: Strong; consistent ACE/Coordinator API/chain-selector terminology, unambiguous prose. No action needed.

audit.summary: This is a "Supported Networks" reference page for Chainlink ACE (private beta) whose two core sections — `## Mainnet networks` and `## Testnet networks` — are **empty**: the page promises "ACE Beta is available on the following networks" and then lists none. Its one genuine strength is the crisp, liftable chain-selector definition. The single biggest opportunity is trivially obvious and high-impact: populate the network sections with a table (network name, chain selector, chain ID, mainnet/testnet, status). Until that content exists, the page cannot be retrieved or cited to answer the exact question its title implies — no metadata or prose polish can compensate for the missing payload.

recommendations.title: Populate the empty network sections with a table
recommendations.issue: Both sections are empty; "available on the following networks" lists none.
recommendations.change: Add a table under each heading with columns: Network name, Chain selector (numeric), Chain ID, Status (live/beta). E.g. a row per supported chain. This is the page's entire reason to exist.
recommendations.why: Named networks + numeric selectors/IDs are the exact liftable facts engines cite; an empty section cannot be retrieved or synthesized for its own topic.

recommendations.title: Add an answer-first summary sentence naming the networks
recommendations.where: Intro line "ACE Beta is available on the following networks."
recommendations.issue: Sentence promises a list that never appears in liftable form.
recommendations.change: Replace with a self-contained lead, e.g. "ACE Beta supports N mainnet and M testnet networks, including [X, Y, Z]; each is identified by a Chainlink chain selector." Front-load the count and names.
recommendations.why: The first liftable sentence must answer "which networks?" verbatim so skimmed/parametric answers stay accurate.

recommendations.title: Add symptom/query-phrased subheadings
recommendations.where: New H3s beneath the section headings.
recommendations.issue: No content phrased as devs/agents ask ("Is ACE on Ethereum mainnet?", "What chain selector does ACE use for Base Sepolia?").
recommendations.change: Add a short "How do I find a network's chain selector?" note linking selectors to the table, and phrase headings around lookup intent.
recommendations.why: Symptom/lookup-phrased sections win retrieval that concept-titled prose loses.

recommendations.title: Add JSON-LD `TechArticle` schema and canonical URL
recommendations.change: Emit a `TechArticle` block with `headline`, `dateModified: 2026-05-26`, `inLanguage`, and a self-referencing `canonical`.
recommendations.why: Structured metadata + canonical raise agent parse-ability and E-E-A-T trust.

recommendations.title: Add an external/primary citation for chain selectors
recommendations.issue: 0 external links; the selector concept is asserted, not attributable.
recommendations.change: Inline-link the canonical CCIP chain-selector directory / registry where the full selector list lives.
recommendations.why: Linking the primary source raises citation rate and lets agents resolve selectors they need.

antiPatterns: **Empty sections under populated headings** — `## Mainnet networks` and `## Testnet networks` are content stubs; this is the dominant defect, not stylistic.
**Promise-without-payload** — "available on the following networks" with no following networks is an unresolved forward reference for a reader/engine.
No keyword stuffing, fluff, or wall-of-prose issues; prose that exists is clean.
offPageNotes: Site-level `llms.txt` is already referenced from the page — good; ensure this URL is listed in it.
JSON-LD/canonical injection is template-level; the CLI should pass raw `<head>` so schema and canonical can be verified rather than assumed absent.
If network availability changes during beta, keep the visible `Last Updated` cadence tight — freshness is a trust signal for a volatile beta list.
